flashcard_questions.q: What is a cult of personality?
flashcard_questions.a: Exaggerated adoration of a leader, built by propaganda to make them seem god-like.

flashcard_questions.q: Which title replaces plain ‘Napoleon’ by Chapter Eight?
Why are Napoleon’s grand epithets satirical?
flashcard_questions.a: They contradict each other — he cannot be both a terror and a ducklings’ friend.

flashcard_questions.q: Which bird marches in front of Napoleon as a kind of trumpeter?
Who writes the poem ‘Comrade Napoleon’ praising the leader?
Which bathetic line in that poem deflates its religious tone?
Where is the poem painted in relation to the Seven Commandments?
flashcard_questions.a: On the barn wall opposite them, beside Napoleon’s portrait.

flashcard_questions.q: Which farmer pays Napoleon for the timber with forged banknotes?
What do Frederick’s men use to destroy the windmill?
Which name does Napoleon give the battle against Frederick’s men?
Which decoration does Napoleon create and then award to himself?
flashcard_questions.a: The Order of the Green Banner.

flashcard_questions.q: Which real betrayal does Frederick’s attack parallel?
flashcard_questions.a: Hitler breaking the Nazi-Soviet Pact by invading the Soviet Union in 1941.

flashcard_questions.q: Which item of Mr Jones’s clothing does the drunken Napoleon wear?
Which two words are added to the Fifth Commandment about alcohol?
What is spin in political communication?
flashcard_questions.a: A deliberately misleading presentation of events, used to control public perception.

notes: 15 cards: 8 text-detail fronts (the new title, the cockerel, Minimus, the swill-bucket line, Frederick, the blasting powder, the Green Banner, the bowler hat), 2 term-to-definition (cult of personality, spin), 2 technique-to-effect (the contradictory epithets, the poem’s placement), 1 context parallel (the Nazi-Soviet Pact), 2 commandment/naming cards (Battle of the Windmill, ‘to excess’). ‘Epithets’, ‘deification’, ‘satire’, ‘totalitarian’, ‘irony’ and ‘blasting powder’ dropped as glossary restatements or too mutually similar to self-grade. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
